note: On starting point he is close to ideal and articulates the good-to-great framing better than almost anyone in the batch: 'if I get absolutely shredded, amazing, but I'm really looking for the longevity aspects' and 'I feel like where I'm at, I can maintain for a long time, but I want to go past that.' He is health-literate and active — e-bike commute, walking treadmill, organic eating, ad-hoc kettlebell work — and nowhere near the deconditioned exclusion. He fails both commercial criteria and fails them hard. A youth minister at a church is not a business owner, physician or equivalent, and the financial picture the rep properly elicited is decisive: about $4-5K liquid, one credit card with about the same available, a recent house move, a young child, and a household rule requiring a joint conversation on anything over $100. This is the mirror image of the Grant Childress call the same day: near-identical goals and starting point, opposite commercial profile, opposite outcome. It supports the existing observation that income is doing most of the real screening work, and suggests the ICP would be more useful if it said so directly rather than bundling income with occupation.
